people.label: Timothy Floyd Burchett
people.sub: U.S. Rep. (R-TN-2); House Oversight; founder, Congressional UAP Caucus
people.narrative: Burchett is the member who forced the modern UAP record into the open. He and Anna Paulina Luna drove the 26 July 2023 House Oversight National Security subcommittee hearing into existence; Ranking Member Robert Garcia thanked him from the dais for the leadership 'that has brought us to this place today,' and Jared Moskowitz did the same. Burchett opened that hearing by putting the first documented stonewall on the record: 'we were even denied access to a classified briefing in a SCIF prior to this hearing due to the amount of hoops that we had to jump through to grant temporary clearance to witness Grusch.' He then used his rounds to ask Grusch the questions no one else would - whether people had been harmed or murdered in the course of concealment (Grusch: 'Yes, personally,' and on murder, 'I have to be careful answering that question. I directed people with that knowledge to the appropriate authorities'), and what Special Access Programs cover the material and how they evaded oversight (Grusch: 'I do know the names'). Every one of those answers terminated at a SCIF the committee was not allowed into. He launched the bipartisan Congressional UAP Caucus in August 2023 and led a caucus letter to the Intelligence Community Inspector General; in January 2024 he brought roughly sixteen members to a closed ICIG briefing with Thomas Monheim and rated it a four out of ten - 'more of the same... it's very compartmentalized; it's like looking down the barrel of a .22 rifle.' He led the first push for a UAP select committee under Speaker McCarthy, which died with the speakership. He is the author of every standalone House UAP bill that matters: H.R. 8424 and H.R. 1187 (UAP Transparency Act) and H.R. 10111 and H.R. 5060 (UAP Whistleblower Protection Act). None have received a markup. His structural theory of the concealment is explicit and it is the theory this board is built on: 'You have to imagine Oak Ridge National Laboratory, the Manhattan Project, thousands of people working on the atomic bomb and less than 12 knew what it was.'
people.tierRationale: Tier A: the originating actor of the House disclosure record, named on the dais by both parties as such, and the first member to put a denial-of-SCIF-access on a sworn hearing record.

people.sub: U.S. Rep. (R-FL-13); Chairwoman, Task Force on the Declassification of Federal Secrets
people.narrative: Luna is the member who converted House UAP interest into a standing institutional instrument. She was waived onto the July 2023 subcommittee and used her rounds to establish two things on the record that the committee has pursued ever since: that Grusch had received DoD Prepublication and Security Review approval for what he was saying, and that he feared for his life. On 11 February 2025 Oversight Chairman James Comer created the Task Force on the Declassification of Federal Secrets and put her in the chair; she and Comer sent letters to Secretary of State Marco Rubio, Secretary of Defense Pete Hegseth and CIA Director John Ratcliffe demanding a briefing on all UAP records in their possession. On 9 September 2025 she chaired the third House UAP hearing and used her opening statement to document the concealment architecture in plain language - that DoD told committee staff that under special access program rules only members of the House Armed Services Committee and the Defense Subcommittee of Appropriations could be read in, and that any other member needed the approval of the chairman and ranking member of both. That is the mechanism: an Oversight committee with subpoena power told it lacks the clearance jurisdiction to see what it is investigating. In the same statement she called former AARO director Sean Kirkpatrick 'a documented liar' and read Christopher Mellon's assessment of AARO's historical report into the record. On 1 April 2026 she wrote Secretary Hegseth demanding AARO's unreleased UAP video files after whistleblowers told the Task Force they exist; the Department blew the deadline in mid-April 2026 and she publicly raised the subpoena. On 9 June 2026 she called on the White House to grant immunity to whistleblowers willing to name locations of recovered craft and technology.
people.tierRationale: Tier A: chairs the only standing House body with a UAP declassification remit, and put the DoD SAP read-in gate on the public record as the specific mechanism blocking Oversight.

people.narrative: Burlison is the member who took the disclosure fight off the witness table and onto the contractors. You have got to show me' - and used his round to test whether the recovered material could be domestic, which Grusch denied. He then radicalised on the process rather than the phenomenon. In March 2024 he led a bipartisan call for a House select committee on UAP focused first on the money, and said flatly that DoD lied to members in a classified setting: 'They weren't transparent to us in a SCIF setting. In March 2025 he hired David Grusch as a senior adviser on UAP matters for a four-month term - the whistleblower moving inside the legislative branch. At the 9 September 2025 hearing he publicly unveiled, for the first time, footage he says shows an MQ-9 firing a Hellfire missile at an orb off Yemen on 30 October 2024, and put two further stonewalls on the record: that his UAP disclosure amendment to the NDAA had been ruled non-germane 'mostly deemed by staff, not even an elected official,' and that in 2024 'we were blocked by someone in House administration from being able to receive a full briefing from AARO.' In 2026 he turned the investigation onto the FFRDC layer, writing MIT Lincoln Laboratory in May 2026 for a classified 1952 'flying saucer talk' briefing recording (their attorneys agreed to comply within 30 days) and MITRE on 22 May 2026 with a ten-page demand covering over forty production categories and records back to 1930. His stated theory: 'If you really want to hide something from Congress, you don't put it in a government file cabinet. You hand it to a private contractor. That's why my investigation is following the trail into RAND, MITRE, Aerospace Corp, MIT Lincoln Labs, and the Northrop Grummans of the world.' In April 2026 he and Chairman Comer opened the congressional probe into the deaths and disappearances of scientists tied to sensitive research, triggered by the vanishing of retired Air Force Gen. William Neil McCasland.

people.narrative: Ocasio-Cortez asked the most technically precise question of the 2023 hearing and it is the one that has aged best. Waived onto the subcommittee, she framed the committee as a whistleblower-protection body and then went at the funding mechanism rather than the phenomenon. Her line of questioning concerned Independent Research and Development - the mechanism by which defense contractors recover the cost of self-directed research from the government - and the statutory notification requirements attached to it. She told Grusch she had personally seen defense contractors abuse their contracts through this committee and seen congressional notification requirements abused, and identified the loophole: 'there are no actual definitions or requirements for notification.' She then pressed on the operational reality of that loophole - when an agency says it notified Congress, does it call the chairman of a committee, or is it 'an email to, hypothetically, a dead email box?' That is the question of whether the congressional notification that legally legitimates a waived unacknowledged program is a real event or a formality. She closed her round by asking all three witnesses, for the record, where she should look - 'titles, programs, departments, regions.' She attended the 12 January 2024 closed ICIG briefing.

entities.desc: The House's general-purpose investigative committee, styled Committee on Oversight and Accountability in the 118th Congress and Committee on Oversight and Government Reform in the 119th, chaired by James Comer since 2023 with Jamie Raskin and then Robert Garcia as ranking member. It is the only House committee with government-wide investigative jurisdiction and unilateral subpoena authority in the chair's hands, which is why the UAP question landed here rather than in Armed Services or Intelligence. It has held every House UAP hearing of the modern era: 26 July 2023 through its National Security, the Border, and Foreign Affairs subcommittee; 13 November 2024 as a joint hearing of that subcommittee and the Cybersecurity, Information Technology and Government Innovation subcommittee; and 9 September 2025 through the Task Force on the Declassification of Federal Secrets. Its structural problem is stated in its own record. On 9 September 2025 Chairwoman Luna disclosed that DoD had told committee staff that under special access program rules only House Armed Services and Defense Appropriations members could be read in on the relevant programs, and that any other member required approval from the chairman and ranking member of both. The committee that can subpoena cannot be cleared; the committees that are cleared have not subpoenaed. That is the load-bearing structural fact of the entire House disclosure effort.

entities.label: The HASC/HAC-D special access program read-in gate
entities.desc: The specific bureaucratic mechanism by which the committee with subpoena power is kept away from the material it is investigating, stated on the record by the chair of the House body investigating it. On 9 September 2025 Anna Paulina Luna told the hearing that in preparation for previous UAP hearings the committee repeatedly asked the Department of Defense to allow members to view UAP videos and files, and that DoD notified committee staff that under the Department's special access program rules only members of the House Armed Services Committee and the Defense Subcommittee of House Appropriations could be read in on such programmes; for any non-committee member to view the documents and videos, individual members must be approved by the chairman AND ranking member of BOTH HASC and HAC-D. Luna added that independent staff oversight is a consistent problem because programme budgets are classified and oversight reporting to Congress goes only to the authorising and appropriating committees of jurisdiction. This is the operative architecture: it is not a refusal, it is a jurisdictional routing that makes refusal unnecessary. Eric Burlison supplied two further instances of the same pattern in the same hearing - an NDAA UAP disclosure amendment ruled non-germane 'mostly deemed by staff, not even an elected official,' and members blocked in 2024 from a full AARO briefing by 'someone in House administration.' The Holman Rule threat Ogles made in 2023 and the subpoena Gaetz asked for in 2023 and Luna raised in 2026 are the only instruments that route around this gate, and none has been used.

entities.sub: Comer-Burlison investigation; triggered by Gen. McCasland
entities.desc: On 20-21 April 2026 Oversight Chairman James Comer and Rep. Eric Burlison, chair of the Subcommittee on Economic Growth, Energy Policy and Regulatory Affairs, opened a congressional investigation into eleven people working in nuclear or rocket technology who have died or vanished under unexplained circumstances since 2022. The trigger was the disappearance in February 2026 of retired Air Force Maj. Gen. William Neil McCasland, former commander of the Air Force Research Laboratory at Wright-Patterson, from his Albuquerque home, leaving behind his phone, glasses, hiking boots, wallet and a .38-calibre revolver. Burlison revealed that his own staff had been trying to reach McCasland about a separate congressional investigation before he disappeared. The committee demanded briefings from the FBI, the Department of War, NASA and the Department of Energy by 27 April 2026; reporting on 28 April indicated the deadline passed without FBI answers. This is the point at which The Program and The Vanishing become the same investigation: the House committee running the UAP inquiry is now also running the missing-scientists inquiry, and the two were connected by the same member and the same disappearance.

entities.desc: On 9 June 2026 lawmakers and UAP whistleblowers gathered at the US Capitol to renew demands for transparency, with David Grusch returning to the Hill for the first time since his 2023 testimony. The specific asks were sharper than at any hearing: Anna Paulina Luna said lawmakers were requesting that the White House grant immunity to whistleblowers who come forward with information including the locations of UAP craft and advanced technology; Eric Burlison echoed the immunity call and asked President Trump to waive all non-disclosure agreements for UAP whistleblowers, while describing a 'Tom Clancy-style dead drop' of information to his office. The American people deserve to know.' Burchett said a congressional tour of Area 51 would yield a T-shirt because the government would move everything else first. Lawmakers also called for the release of records relating to the 1996 Varginha incident in Brazil. The recurring theme was money and oversight rather than biology: whether the Pentagon is spending outside congressional reach.

entities.label: FY2026 NDAA UAP provisions
entities.sub: Three AARO directives; conference version Dec 2025
entities.desc: The fiscal 2026 National Defense Authorization Act carried three UAP provisions directed at AARO. First, a required briefing to lawmakers on UAP intercepts by the integrated commands defending North America - NORAD and US Northern Command - going back to 2004, specifying the number, location and nature of intercepts and the data collected or analysed during them. Second, an accounting for UAP-related security classification guides used in reports and investigations, aimed squarely at overclassification and improper restriction of imagery and data. Third, the elimination of duplicative reporting requirements and streamlining of how agencies supply data to AARO. The Disclosure Foundation characterised these as a meaningful if incremental step and noted that two of the three mirror recommendations championed by Christopher Mellon. The classification-guide provision is the most consequential for this board: a security classification guide is the document that tells a programme what to stamp, and compelling its production is the first step toward proving that the stamping was improper.

entities.label: PURSUE - Presidential Unsealing and Reporting System for UAP Encounters
entities.sub: Executive disclosure channel announced Feb 2026; first drop 8 May 2026
entities.desc: The executive branch's answer to the congressional demand, and therefore the thing the House caucus has to measure. President Trump announced on 19-20 February 2026 that he would direct Secretary of Defense Pete Hegseth and relevant agencies to 'begin the process of identifying and releasing Government files related to alien and extraterrestrial life, unidentified aerial phenomena (UAP), and unidentified flying objects (UFOs).' The resulting mechanism, PURSUE, is coordinated by AARO and publishes through a war.gov portal. The first drop on 8 May 2026 contained roughly 160 declassified files, at least 100 of them redacted, including pilot reports, descriptions of metallic spheres, discs and orbs, Apollo 12 and 17 records, FBI orb reports from 2023 and footage from Greece. Christopher Mellon's verdict is the one the House caucus has adopted: 'Data alone is not disclosure. Releasing raw files without context may confuse more than clarify.' Alejandro Rojas noted the case summaries lacked coordinates, sensor parameters and altitude data; Tim Gallaudet said the absence of metadata made it impossible to conclude any object was truly anomalous. The House response has been to keep sending letters - Luna's to Hegseth in April 2026, Burlison's to MITRE and Lincoln Laboratory in May 2026 - on the premise that an executive-controlled release cannot substitute for compelled production.

entities.sub: USAF installation; site of the 2023 protected disclosure
entities.desc: The Air Force installation in Florida's first congressional district that produced the only UAP incident a member of Congress has personally investigated on site. Matt Gaetz's office received a protected disclosure from Eglin; he travelled there with Burchett and Luna and was initially refused images, radar and full flight-crew access before obtaining a photograph and an interview with one crew member. The incident involved a test mission over the Gulf of Mexico in airspace that was supposed to be clear, and a formation of four craft in a diamond plus an orb. Gaetz described the radar sequence as one he alone in Congress had seen and asked that the material be subpoenaed. Luna returned to Eglin in her September 2025 opening statement, describing 'the infamous Eglin Air Force Base incident' and stating that multiple active-duty Air Force pilot whistleblowers alleged that the Air Force was covering up UAP activity there. As of August 2026 the Eglin radar and imagery have not been produced to the committee.

sap-readin-gate.desc: The full text of the mechanism as stated by Chairwoman Luna on 9 September 2025: 'A major barrier to this Committee's inquiry into UAPs has been the lack of cooperation and transparency from the Department of Defense and the intelligence community. In preparation for previous UAP hearings, the Committee repeatedly asked the Department of Defense to allow members to view videos and files related to UAP incidences. Unfortunately, the Department of Defense notified the Committee staff that, due to the Department's special access program rules, only members of the House Armed Services Committee, as well as the Defense Subcommittee on House Appropriations, also known as HAC-D, were allowed to be read in onto such programs. For a non-committee member to be allowed to view these documents and videos, individual members must be approved by the Chairman and Ranking Member of both HASC and HAC-D. Independent staff oversight has presented a consistent problem for Congress, as well as program budgets are classified. Additionally, oversight reporting to Congress is classified and only provided to the authorizing and Appropriations Committees of jurisdiction.' Read alongside Burchett's July 2023 disclosure that members were denied a SCIF briefing before the founding hearing, Burlison's account of being blocked from a full AARO briefing by House Administration staff in 2024 and of his NDAA amendment being ruled non-germane by staff in 2025, and Gaetz's account of being refused the Eglin radar until he raised how authorities flow, the pattern is consistent: access is not refused on the merits, it is routed away on jurisdiction and procedure.

hearing-2025-09-09.desc: Beyond the headline moments, the 9 September 2025 record contains three further items worth preserving. Burlison entered into the record witness testimonies supplied to him by Dr. Steven Greer, naming Michael Herrera, Roderick Castle, Randy Anderson and Steven Digna among others. Burlison also stated on the record that the UAP Disclosure Act 'was stripped out by the House last year, and I cannot get it onto the bill leaving the House this year,' which is the House-side counterpart to the Senate story of the UAPDA's gutting. And Ranking Member Crockett placed the whole subject inside the documented history of American overclassification - MLK and Malcolm X, COINTELPRO, the torture programs - which is the framing that makes the inquiry survivable across party control.

gaps: No published charter or full member roster for the Congressional UAP Caucus was located. Members are established only piecemeal from contemporaneous reporting (Burchett, Luna, Burlison, Moskowitz, Ogles). The caucus letter to the ICIG of 22 August 2023 has not been located in full text - obtaining it would fix both the roster and the specific asks.

The 12-page Immaculate Constellation document entered into the Congressional Record on 13 November 2024 has not been located as a retrievable primary file at a stable URL. It is referenced in the hearing's Index of Documents as available at docs.house.gov; retrieving it is the single highest-value document task in this domain.

Rep. Crane's 24 July 2025 letter to the Secretary of Defense on the Grusch reprisal, entered into the record on 9 September 2025, has not been located in full text. It is the only congressional document enumerating the specific adverse actions taken against Grusch.

Rep. Burlison's 22 May 2026 ten-page MITRE letter and his May 2026 MIT Lincoln Laboratory letter have not been located in full text; only DefenseScoop's and The Hill's descriptions of them. The 40+ production categories in the MITRE letter would be a map of what a member of Congress believes an FFRDC holds.
Chairwoman Luna's 1 April 2026 letter to Secretary Hegseth is referenced by the committee's own release as linked but the letter file itself was not retrieved.

No House UAP hearing appears to have been held between 9 September 2025 and 12 August 2026. Whether one is scheduled, and whether the Task Force's remit survives into the next Congress, is unresolved.

Rep. Mike Gallagher: no UAP-specific statement, letter, amendment or briefing attendance was located. He is retained as a node only because he held simultaneously the HASC and HPSCI seats that constitute the read-in tier from which Oversight was excluded. His actual UAP posture, if any, is unknown.
The identity and disposition of the 'certain individuals who did not want this hearing to happen' referenced by Chairwoman Mace on 13 November 2024 is not on the record. Mace declined to name them.

Whether the House Oversight Committee has ever issued a UAP-related subpoena is not affirmatively established; the finding here is a negative inferred from the absence of any such subpoena in the three hearing records and in committee releases through August 2026. A direct check of the committee's subpoena log would settle it.

The Eglin AFB radar sequence and flight-crew photograph Gaetz described in July 2023, and asked be subpoenaed, have never been produced to the committee so far as the record shows. The incident date, unit and aircraft type are not on the public record.

The scope of the 'separate congressional investigation' for which Rep. Burlison's staff were trying to reach Gen. William Neil McCasland before his February 2026 disappearance has not been publicly specified. This is the sharpest open question linking this board to The Vanishing.

Rep. Nick Begich, Rep. Dina Titus, Rep. Summer Lee, Rep. Dave Min, Rep. Brandon Gill and Rep. Nick Langworthy all participated in one or more of the three hearings or sit on the Task Force but were not given dossiers here for space. Each is a legitimate node.

The FY2026 NDAA UAP provisions were described from reporting on the conference version; the enacted statutory text and section numbers were not retrieved and should be pinned before any of the three provisions is cited as law.
